objective: Incorporating approved risk-mitigation activities into the schedule under formal change control, establishing a new PMB
secondaryObjectives: Updating the schedule model and documenting baseline changes through formal change-control processes

sources.cite: PMI, PMI Scheduling Professional (PMI-SP) Examination Content Outline (2012, revision mark 4/20): Schedule Strategy 14%, Planning and Development 31%, Monitoring and Controlling 35%, Closeout 6%, Stakeholder Communications 14%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a consultancy. Relevant text: Monitoring and Controlling Task 3 'Perform schedule analysis and audit ... in order to identify and report project schedule, status, changes, impacts or issues'; Task 5 'Incorporate approved risk mitigation activities into the schedule, by utilizing defined change control processes'; Task 6 'Update the schedule model and document schedule baseline changes, received through formal change-control processes'. The objective wording here is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's clinic-fitout-variance-pmisp (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the scheduler on a fictional hospital laboratory refit for Northgate Health. The risk board approved two mitigations last month: a second commissioning crew and a pre-delivery inspection of the analyzers.
handover: The approved mitigations add 3 weeks of activities and 180 thousand dollars.
Neither is in the schedule; the baseline still shows the original finish.
howItWorks: The dashboard shows the commitments, the work items, the risks and issues, the people's support and the milestones.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each status meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: the sponsor sees a 3-week slip with no approved change behind it and halts reporting.
Week 3: an audit cannot reconcile the finish date with any approved change; the contractor disputes a delay claim.
Week 4: hospital departments plan a move for the original date; the lab is not ready and patient tests are delayed.

crPrompt.title: Approved mitigations outside the schedule
crPrompt.context: The work is approved but not scheduled.

choices.label: Raise a change request with the activities, durations, costs and logic links for both mitigations, for the change board
choices.feedback: Approved risk responses enter the schedule through formal change control, like any scope change.

choices.label: Add the mitigations as notes on existing activities
choices.feedback: The work is mentioned but not scheduled, resourced or linked.

choices.label: Insert the activities into the live schedule without a change request
choices.feedback: The baseline and the live schedule now disagree with no record why.

rebaselinePrompt.title: Which baseline to measure against
rebaselinePrompt.context: The change is approved; the old baseline remains.

choices.label: Update the schedule model and set a new performance measurement baseline, keeping the original for history and recording the change number

effects.log: A new baseline is set; the history is kept.

choices.feedback: An approved change updates the baseline formally, with the change documented and the original kept.

choices.label: Keep measuring against the original baseline
choices.feedback: Every report now shows a 3-week variance that was approved.

choices.label: Overwrite the original baseline with no record
choices.feedback: Nobody can tell what changed, when or why.

choices.label: Report status against the new baseline and show the approved change that moved the finish, with its reason

effects.log: The sponsor sees an on-plan project and why the date moved.

choices.feedback: Status reports show variance against the current baseline and trace approved changes.

choices.label: Report only the new finish date
choices.feedback: Correct, but stakeholders may think the project slipped.

choices.label: Report the original finish until the mitigations are done
choices.feedback: The report promises a date the schedule no longer supports.

scoring.modelReasoning: Approved risk responses are work: they enter the schedule through formal change control, the schedule model is updated, and a new performance measurement baseline is set with the change documented and the original kept. Status is then reported against the current baseline, with approved changes traced.
